title: Update pricing playbook: approvals matrix, experimental bands, and security questionnaire tie-ins
creator: Asha Menon
description: Objective: Consolidate and publish a single-source pricing playbook that 1) defines approval thresholds for discounts and credits, 2) documents experiment bands for A/B price tests and limited pilot pricing, and 3) maps answers in the enterprise security questionnaire (SAQ) to pricing and contracting constraints. Deliverable: published playbook in Confluence, a one-page cheat sheet for sales, and an initial set of email templates for approved discount responses.
background: We currently have fragmented guidance across a Google Sheet (pricebook), several sales play decks, and ad-hoc email templates. Enterprise contracts and Security Questionnaires (SQs) often introduce bespoke clauses that sales interprets as reasons to approve larger discounts or custom legal terms. That inconsistency increases deal cycle time and leakage. This ticket centralizes governance and establishes lightweight experiment controls to measure price elasticity on pilot accounts.
problem_statement: No single canonical source defines who can approve price concessions, how to handle SQ-driven custom terms that carry compliance/cost risk, or how to run small-scale pricing experiments without invalidating book-of-record reporting.
proposed_solution: 1) Approval matrix: define by ARR band, product offering (hosted/dedicated/private), and security classification. 2) Experiment bands: create two experimental discount bands (Pilot: up to 15% for <6 months with compensation clauses; TrialPromo: one-time 10% for self-serve expansion) with tracking tags and expiration. 3) SQ integration: annotate pricebook rows with SQ flags (data residency, encryption/KMS, on-prem) and required legal signoffs. 4) Publish templates and enforcement checklist for finance/legal approvals.

Initial retrospective planned after 30 closed deals using experiment bands
